questions.prompt: Match each item to the folder it belongs in.

pairs.left: A presentational Badge component and a duration pipe
DiaryStore and the diary edit page

questions.explanation: core/ holds app-wide singletons and the shell, shared/ holds feature-agnostic building blocks, and each feature folder holds its own pages and state.

questions.prompt: The diary feature needs an exercise picker that currently lives in features/exercises. What should you do?

options.text: Import it directly from ../exercises/exercise-picker
Copy the file into the diary folder and keep both in sync
Move the picker to shared/ if it's generic, so both features import it from there
Merge the two features into one folder

questions.explanation: Features shouldn't import from each other. A generic, reusable piece belongs in shared/; an app-wide service belongs in core/.

questions.prompt: app.routes.ts uses loadComponent for the diary page, but the page still appears in the main bundle. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Lazy loading only works in development builds
The page is also imported statically somewhere that the main bundle includes, such as the top of app.routes.ts
loadComponent only works with NgModules
The page component is missing standalone: true

questions.explanation: A single static import pulls the code back into the main bundle. Keep feature code behind dynamic import() calls only. (Standalone is the default since Angular 19.)

questions.prompt: Which route property registers a service shared by a route and all of its child routes?
questions.explanation: Route-level providers create an injector for that route subtree, so every page in the feature gets the same instance without using the root injector.

questions.prompt: Which tools help keep bundles small as the app grows? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Size budgets in angular.json
withPreloading(PreloadAllModules) for background loading of lazy chunks
@defer for heavy, non-critical parts of a page
A SHARED_IMPORTS array spread into every component

questions.explanation: Budgets catch growth, preloading and @defer keep the first load small. A giant shared imports array does the opposite: every component depends on everything.

questions.prompt: What is the standalone-era version of the 'single-module app' anti-pattern?

options.text: Using loadComponent instead of loadChildren
One shared imports list (or one flat folder) that every component depends on
Using route-level providers
Using path aliases like @shared/*

questions.explanation: Both anti-patterns remove boundaries: everything depends on everything, so nothing can be found, split, or owned separately.

questions.prompt: What does @defer (on viewport; prefetch on idle) { <app-chart /> } @placeholder { … } do?

options.text: Renders the chart immediately and hides it until scrolled into view
Downloads the chart's code when the browser is idle, and renders it when the placeholder scrolls into view
Loads the chart on the server only
Lazy-loads the whole route

questions.explanation: prefetch on idle fetches the code early without rendering it; on viewport renders it once the placeholder becomes visible.
